definition: ROCm is an Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) software stack for graphics processing unit (GPU) programming.
details: ROCm spans several domains, including general-purpose computing on graphics processing units (GPGPU), high-performance computing (HPC), and heterogeneous computing. It offers several programming models: HIP (GPU-kernel-based programming), OpenMP (directive-based programming), and OpenCL. ROCm is free, libre and open-source software (except the GPU firmware blobs), and it is distributed under various licenses. The name initially stood for Radeon Open Compute platform; however, due to Open Compute being a registered trademark, the name no longer functions as an acronym.

explainer.lead: ROCm is AMD's open software stack for programming its GPUs. It matters as the main open alternative to vendor-specific GPU compute platforms for general-purpose GPU work.

tiers.eli5: It's the set of tools that lets your computer hand heavy number-crunching jobs to an AMD graphics card, similar to a driver kit for computing.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to run GPGPU and HPC workloads on AMD hardware via HIP, OpenMP, or OpenCL. A pitfall is that library support and hardware compatibility vary, so porting code is not always drop-in.
tiers.paperLevel: ROCm is free, libre and open-source software except the GPU firmware blobs, distributed under various licenses, spanning GPGPU, HPC, and heterogeneous computing with HIP, OpenMP, and OpenCL programming models; the name initially stood for Radeon Open Compute platform.

explainer.example: A team ports a HIP kernel to an AMD GPU using ROCm to run a parallel compute job.
